question: Can a literal Q table be arranged as progressive exact lookup layers so a consumer pays first for the decision signal it actually asks for?
layers: layer 2: exact runner-up action and exact best-to-runner-up score gap
layers 3 through 9: each next action and adjacent exact score gap
final calibration layer: exact maximum Q value for full absolute reconstruction

acceptance.top_two: zero runner-up or best-to-runner-up gap mismatches on every row with at least two admissible actions
acceptance.full_table: zero permitted-score or forbidden-mask mismatches after loading every layer
acceptance.top_two_prefix_bytes: complete header plus required streams must not exceed 60000 bytes
acceptance.fail_closed: wrong source, wrong magic, and corrupted stream must be rejected

exploratory_disclosure: The 60000-byte top-two threshold follows an exploratory in-memory stream-size probe. It is an engineering acceptance limit, not a fresh statistical discovery threshold.
nonclaims: A top-k prefix does not preserve lower-ranked alternatives or absolute return.
Only the complete artifact reconstructs the full source table exactly.
Progressive access trades a larger full artifact for smaller task-specific prefixes.
The representation does not improve the source policy or add learned knowledge.
The result is specific to this compiled synthetic table and implemented controls.
